title: How a Tsunami Races Across the Ocean
description: What sets off a tsunami, how fast it travels and how it behaves near shore, from NOAA and USGS.
narration: What turns an underwater shake into a giant wave? Tsunamis are waves set off by undersea earthquakes or volcanic eruptions. Coastal landslides that dump huge amounts of debris into the water can set them off as well. NOAA says they may match the speed of jet planes. The speed of a tsunami depends on ocean depth, not on distance from the source. They slow down only when they reach shallow water. Near shore, it behaves like an extremely fast tide that pushes much farther inland. And it usually arrives as several waves, not just one.
